summary: Task 4 ships test-only fixture infrastructure. The hardcoded 32-byte Ed25519 seed is properly isolated behind a default-OFF cargo feature (`golden-fixtures`) and an additional integration-test gate (`#![cfg(all(feature = "golden-fixtures", not(target_arch = "wasm32")))]`). Seed cannot reach production binaries. No new runtime dependencies, no shell-injection or path-traversal exposure in the regenerator script (paths are repo-derived from BASH_SOURCE, not user input). The lockstep CI gate correctly catches silent CBOR/COSE encoder drift, which itself is a defense-in-depth control against accidental cryptographic envelope mutation. Two LOW findings only — neither blocks merge.

notes: FIXED_SEED_HEX = 00112233...eeff is documented as test-only ('MUST NOT be used to sign any real attestation') in core/tests/golden_fixtures.rs:55-61.

Seed lives ONLY inside core/tests/golden_fixtures.rs — confirmed via grep across the entire repo (only other occurrence is the matching keypair_secret_hex in the committed fixture JSON, which is the expected test artifact).
core/Cargo.toml:46 sets `default = []`; `golden-fixtures = []` (line 60) is opt-in, not in the default feature set.

Native and WASM release builds do NOT compile core/tests/golden_fixtures.rs because (a) `tests/` is only built under `cargo test`, and (b) the file has `#![cfg(all(feature = "golden-fixtures", not(target_arch = "wasm32")))]` as defense in depth.
Ed25519 is RFC 8032 deterministic, so the fixed seed produces stable signatures — no reliance on a random source the seed could mask. No reuse of nonces (Ed25519 doesn't have user-supplied nonces).
The pinned 32-byte seed is intentional and a security-positive: it makes the lockstep gate detectable. A random-per-run seed would defeat byte-for-byte comparison.

Feature flag `golden-fixtures` is OFF by default (core/Cargo.toml:46-60). `cargo build --workspace` in CI/release does not enable it — confirmed by grepping .github/ for `--all-features` (no match) and `golden-fixtures` (only appears in the dedicated lockstep job).
The release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml — out of T4 scope but checked) does not enable the feature.

Test seed is never used to sign real attestations — `sign_cose` consumers in production code paths receive keypairs from `Keypair::generate()` or `import_keypair_json` originating from user-controlled material.

Lockstep design correctly forces fixture regeneration as a coupled commit when the encoder changes, so an attacker who silently mutates `to_canonical_cbor` or `sign_cose` to produce different bytes would also have to regenerate the fixture, which would surface in code review.
The `golden-fixtures` feature only enables the test file body. No new runtime modules, no extra `pub` exports from `core/src/lib.rs`.
No new runtime dependencies in core/Cargo.toml. Existing `serde_json`, `hex`, `solana-sdk`, `chrono` already in the dependency graph.
No new test deps (the test reuses already-present `serde_json`, `serde`, `solana-sdk`, `hex`).

No new npm runtime deps in packages/sdk/package.json. The new test file imports only `vitest` (existing devDep), `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:url` (built-ins), and the local `core/pkg-nodejs/mnemonic_core.js` artifact (workspace-internal).
Note: `pkg-nodejs/` is gitignored and built per-environment; it is not vendored into the repo and not published to npm. Supply-chain surface is unchanged.

The lockstep gate IS the integrity control for this task: `git diff --exit-code` against both the SHA-256 file and the JSON itself catches any divergence between Rust encoder output and the committed fixture (.github/workflows/node-test.yml:62-66).

Belt-and-suspenders: the workflow diffs both `golden-cose.sha256` AND `golden-cose.json` directly. Even if a malicious PR updated only the SHA file but left the JSON stale, the second diff catches it.

Determinism is asserted programmatically by `test_emitter_deterministic` (golden_fixtures.rs:362) and `test_fixed_keypair_pubkey_stable` (line 393), so a regression in `Keypair::from_bytes` derivation would fail-closed.

Caveat (informational, not a finding): the lockstep gate runs on `ubuntu-latest` only. If the Rust encoder ever produced platform-dependent output, a developer regenerating on macOS would commit a fixture CI cannot reproduce. Currently `to_canonical_cbor` and `sign_cose` are pure byte-deterministic, so this is theoretical.

Committed fixture JSON contains `keypair_secret_hex` for every entry. This IS a 64-byte Ed25519 secret, but it is the *test* secret and is intentionally exposed — required for the SDK to reproduce the COSE envelope client-side. The seed half (`00112233...eeff`) is documented as test-only in the source, and the derived pubkey (56LtbqTNScYQqjGpec1TW7himmeeGF1L7cGbDt6BfFuU) is consistent across all 22 entries, confirming determinism.

If a future contributor copies the fixture seed thinking it's safe randomness, they get a clearly-labeled test-only string. The `MUST NOT be used to sign any real attestation` comment in golden_fixtures.rs:58-60 is sufficient documentation. Could be repeated in the README for extra defense (LOW finding below).
No JWTs, OAuth codes, PKCE verifiers, or user secrets in the fixture. Only test-keypair material.
set -euo pipefail (line 20) — fails fast on any error or unset var.
REPO_ROOT is derived from BASH_SOURCE via `cd ... && pwd`, NOT from $1/$2/env. Cannot be influenced by an attacker invoking the script with crafted args.
FIXTURE_JSON is constructed from REPO_ROOT + literal path components — no user input flows into shell commands.

RAW_OUTPUT is captured via $(...) and then exported as RAW_CARGO_OUTPUT for the python3 heredoc (line 44). The python3 heredoc is single-quoted (`<<'PY'`), so no shell expansion happens inside the heredoc body. RAW_CARGO_OUTPUT is read via os.environ.get, never via shell substitution. Safe.
The shasum/sha256sum calls properly quote `$FIXTURE_JSON` (lines 65, 67). Awk pipes are positional (`{print $1}`).
The `git diff --exit-code` lockstep step (node-test.yml:63-66) operates on fixed paths inside the workspace; no user-controlled arguments.

findings.category: A03 / minor robustness — quoting in inline python
findings.issue: $FIXTURE_JSON is interpolated directly into a Python single-quoted string. If a developer happens to place the repo at a path containing a single-quote character (e.g., `/Users/o'brien/src/...`), Python's quoted literal breaks and the script fails — or, in a pathological clone path, could be coerced to evaluate adjacent text. Not a remote injection: the script is local-only and the path is filesystem-derived from BASH_SOURCE. Pure local-developer footgun.
findings.impact: LOW. Not exploitable from a network attacker. At worst, breaks regen in unusual repo paths.
findings.recommendation:
Pass the path via env var, mirroring the safe pattern already used for RAW_CARGO_OUTPUT above:
  FIXTURE_JSON_FOR_PY="$FIXTURE_JSON" python3 -c 'import json,os; print(len(json.load(open(os.environ["FIXTURE_JSON_FOR_PY"]))))'

findings.issue: The fixture JSON exposes the 64-byte test-only Ed25519 keypair (32-byte seed + 32-byte derived pubkey) in plain hex on every entry. This is intentional and required, but the JSON itself contains no inline marker that the value is test-only. A future developer skimming the file (or grep'ing for high-entropy strings) might be confused.
findings.impact: LOW. Documentation/clarity only. No real-world cryptographic risk — the seed is published in the source comment and the derived pubkey will appear in any new git history.
findings.recommendation: Optional: add a top-level metadata comment field to the fixture (e.g., a leading `_meta` object) explicitly tagging the seed as 'TEST_ONLY' and pointing to core/tests/golden_fixtures.rs:55-61. This requires the JSON to become an object instead of an array, which would propagate to cose.golden.test.ts. Lower cost: add a one-line comment in packages/sdk/README.md's 'Golden COSE fixture' section explicitly flagging that the fixture contains a publicly-known test seed and MUST NOT be used to sign real attestations. Tracked as a hardening nice-to-have, not a security defect.

positive_observations: Feature flag is correctly default-OFF and namespaced (core/Cargo.toml:60).
Cfg gate at top of golden_fixtures.rs:28 prevents the file from compiling on wasm32 even if the feature were accidentally enabled.
test_emitter_deterministic + test_fixed_keypair_pubkey_stable provide strong invariants that the lockstep gate relies on.
Lockstep gate diffs BOTH the SHA file and the JSON file (node-test.yml:62-66) — closes the 'forge the SHA, leave JSON stale' loophole.
Regenerator script uses `set -euo pipefail` and properly-scoped path derivation.
Python heredoc uses RAW_CARGO_OUTPUT env-var passthrough (line 44) rather than shell-substituting raw cargo stdout into a python literal — exactly the right pattern.
No new runtime dependencies, no new npm packages, no broadened public surface in core/src/lib.rs.
recommendation: approve — no blocking findings. Optional follow-ups (T4-S1, T4-S2) can be addressed opportunistically or filed to backlog.
